title: Fishing
summary: Bite cues, catches that go straight to your inventory, Fishing stats, Tidescales, rare finds, sea creatures, baits (one per catch), hotspots, rods, sets, Fishing Frenzy and lava fishing in the Nether.

When the bite is a creature, it is pulled out of the water at you and attacks. You cannot miss it: a big warning sign and a

subtitle with its name and level appear in the creature's colour, with a splash at the bobber and a dramatic sound. The rare ones (Night Skimmer, Abyss Warden and the Cinder Leviathan) get a stronger version, and everyone within 48 blocks reads "<name> fished up <creature>!" in chat. Killing it pays
Fishing XP to the player who fished it up
(the numbers in the table, set per creature by its level and rarity), and
Combat XP to whoever kills it

: the body's normal kill XP plus half the creature's Fishing XP (a Drowned Sailor adds 12, an Abyss Warden 450). If you fish it up and kill it yourself you get both, each counted once; if a friend finishes it off, you still get the Fishing XP and they get the Combat XP. The killer also gets the Tidescales and the rare-find rolls. It leaves after two minutes. Which ones can come up depends on your Fishing level, and the odds are by weight. Health and damage are multiples of the body's normal values.
The Abyss Warden is an Elder Guardian body and the rarest catch. The lava creatures are in the lava fishing section below.
Your level only decides which creatures can come up. Sea Creature Chance decides how often one does, so rods, baits and the Deep Lure talent are how you meet more of them.

s.x: Now and then, near someone who holds a fishing rod, a

appears on open water (on lava in the Nether, for the Magmaline Rod): a circle about 4 blocks wide, drawn as a turning ring of glowing particles with a light pillar in the middle and a floating label such as "Hotspot, +30 Fishing Speed, 2:41". It lasts four minutes, then fades. There are never more than two near you, a while passes between new ones, they need real deep water (no puddles) and never appear in the hub.
Each hotspot has one or two buffs: Fishing Speed, Fishing Fortune, Sea Creature Chance, Double Catch or Rare Finds. The buffs apply to a cast
while the bobber is inside the circle
, not to you: cast into it and your bait box shows "Hotspot: ..."; pull the bobber out and they stop. They add to your bait and gear. The numbers are data:

s.x: fishes in the Nether's lava. Hold it in your main or off hand, in the Nether, and cast into lava.
Its bobber floats on lava like on water, cannot burn, and bites with the usual timing and your Fishing Speed.
Lava catches go into your inventory like every catch.
Lava catches give 14 Fishing XP instead of 8. Tidescales, Double Catch and your stats work the same.
